scope: Decide the coverage architecture for HNK romanization after B1-B4. Do not assign arbitrary new Latin units merely to reach 40/40, and do not change phoneme identities, stress, semantics, morphology, grammar or curriculum.
evidence: A1 established that only 20/40 G-IDs currently have governed safe romanization.
B1 affirmed G40 /y/ with safe Y and kept G16 /j/ distinct, so reusing Y for /j/ is prohibited.
No recovered source-backed safe Latin convention was found for the remaining 20 G-IDs during the audit.
G-ID plus IPA already gives a complete, lossless and non-ambiguous representation for all 40 phonemes.
Inventing digraphs now would create orthographic design debt and possible tokenization collisions without improving phonological authority.

options.description: Keep the existing 20 safe romanizations unchanged. For the other 20, G-ID remains the canonical lossless fallback. New human-friendly Latin/ASCII representations may be authored later only through explicit orthography gates with collision/reversibility checks.
options.effect: No romanization mutation now; 20/40 human safe units + 40/40 G-ID coverage; B6 may proceed using G-ID/IPA authority.

options.description: Design and approve Latin letters/digraphs for all 20 currently unmapped phonemes in this phase.
options.effect: Would require a separate collision, reversibility, keyboard and typography design review; not justified by recovered evidence alone.

options.description: Redesign all 40 romanizations, including the 20 already governed.
options.effect: High compatibility risk and outside the minimum-change audit route.
